steps.prompt: New quest: read {quest} (and the code it cites, including the win-the-day-v0 changes just landed). Write the spec to {run}/spec.md following your role card: exact signatures for the new src/pm/ask_build.cljc, the pm.three ground-grid fn, the pm.core wiring (name the functions you hook), the estate :demo-builds block with its four looks written out, numbered test cases with hand-checked expected values, and a who-touches-what table (builder: src/pm/ask_build.cljc, src/pm/three.cljs, src/pm/core.cljs, resources/estate.edn's new :demo-builds block only; tester: new test/pm/ask_build_test.cljs, only adding tests; le-docteur: a TASKS.md row F-2). Reply when it's written.

prompt.un-automate-monde: Spec: {run}/spec.md (quest: {quest}). Implement it in the source files the spec assigns the builder, and nothing else. Run .crew/gate.sh before replying, then write {run}/builder-notes.md as the quest's Done-when says.
prompt.le-testeur: Spec: {run}/spec.md (quest: {quest}). Write its test cases in the test file the spec assigns the tester, and nothing else. The builder is coding in parallel.

steps.prompt: Run the gate (.crew/gate.sh) and write the gate note to {run}/gate-note.md as your role card says.

Review the round's changes against {run}/spec.md and {quest}: git diff for edited files, and read the new files (git status lists them). Check in particular: the new path runs only with DEMO true; the parser is pure and its words are data; the ground map is measured in the browser and never written to a file or shipped; placement goes through pm.lot/place and the existing apply-blueprint-file! path; demo make-real/remove use pm.demo-builds.v1 and ?fresh clears it; the dev build without a bridge still refuses make-real; every look is grounded and clickable; no person, pet or member named in code; no npm deps. Write the review to {run}/review.md.
Spec: {run}/spec.md (quest: {quest}). Make only the documentation edits the spec's who-touches-what table gives le-docteur (if none, change nothing). Reply with git diff --stat of what you changed.
